text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- All newspapers report on the U.S. decision announced in Brussels on Thursday to have only three ex-communist countries -- not including Romania -- as NATO's first new members.
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The government is expected to adopt at a meeting on Friday or Saturday a proposal to scrap the farm tax, the newspaper quotes Finance Minister Mircea Ciumara as saying.
- The newspaper prints draft of the government's plans to revamp the Reform Council, creating a department to coordinate privatisation, restructuring and foreign investments.
ADEVARUL ECONOMIC
- "We are the Central and East European country with the most stable financial system," Finance Minister Mircea Ciumara says in interview.

- Interview with Liviu Marcu, secretary of state at the Industry Ministry, on the strategy of the oil sector after the planned scrapping of the Romanian Oil Company (CRP) under a government decision next month.
BURSA
- Report on Thursday's all-time turnover high on the Bucharest stock exchange.
ADEVARUL
- The newspaper prints details of a new government proposal for levying road tax for freight trucks and tractors.
General:
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI

- Good-bye NATO -- newspaper prints local political leaders' reactions to the U.S. announcement that Washington supports only three countries -- Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary -- for first-wave expansion of the alliance.
- A remote Romanian village in the mountains near Buzau sees a new rush for amber, says newspaper report.
ADEVARUL

- "NATO -- the U.S. guillotine", says newspaper editorial, saying Romania is "on the waiting list" for NATO expansion after the announcement of Washington' stance on the alliance's first expansion to only three members, not including Romania.
-- Bucharest Newsroom, 40-1 3120264
